title: Family of Toronto police shooting victim question police actions
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit has identified John Menga, a 29-year-old father of two, as the victim of a fatal shooting involving two Toronto police officers who are now under investigation.
Yesterday, Menga's family and friends gathered at his home to mourn his death and question the circumstances of the shooting.
"My brother should still be alive," said Menga's 30-year-old brother Resul. "My brother shouldn't have been shot like that," he said.
The Menga family, originally from the Azores, has maintained strong ties to Toronto's Portuguese community. Resul says he has been contacted by several witnesses who claim to have seen the shooting.

According to previously published eyewitness accounts, Menga, who was driving a stolen Jeep with a passenger inside, was shot when he tried to run down two 14 Division police officers who ordered him to stop. The shooting took place at 9:55 p.m. Friday night.
"I think he panicked and he was scared," Menga's 27-year-old wife Rosa said yesterday.
"He was a good father. He loved his kids," said Rosa, who married Menga seven years ago. They have two children, Amanda, 6 and Johnny, 3. "I can't believe he's gone," she said.

The family lived with Menga's mother Roberta in a two-storey home in the city's west end. John was well-liked and often hung out in the area's Portuguese cafs and bars, according to those who knew him.
"Everybody knew he had his problems, but he was still respected and known as a good guy," said one man who knew him for seven years but did not want his name published.

According to sources, police believe Menga and the man who was with him had just finished buying drugs when they were spotted driving a stolen vehicle by two police officers, Constable Paul Lentsch and his partner Constable Bobby Grewal.
Yesterday, Rosa said that despite her husband's criminal record, which includes drug offences, he was no longer involved with drugs and made a living doing seasonal work in construction.

Earlier in the evening a police broadcast had alerted patrolling officers to be on the lookout for a stolen Jeep Cherokee with front- end damage. "The officers spotted the Jeep as a stolen vehicle. It was damaged in the front and the plate (licence plate) number had been broadcast. One of them (the officers) remembered the first few digits and checked," a police source said. After spotting the stolen vehicle, Lentsch and Grewal turned on the cruiser's flashing lights.

The Jeep drove around them along Bloor Street before turning south on Havelock Street, a one-way street going north. The cruiser blocked the entrance to Havelock and the Jeep reversed, then turned around and drove towards the cruiser.

Before the Jeep collided with the cruiser both constables moved to get out of the car. At that point, Lentsch a 4 1/2 year veteran of the force, and Grewal, who has been on the force for six months, drew their guns and ordered Menga to get out.

Lentsch was then struck by the Jeep and fell to the ground, according to a police source. Both officers then fired a total of seven times. Two bullets fired at the side of the Jeep entered Menga's head through the cheek and one hit his thigh.
Menga died at St. Michael's Hospital. Lentsch has recovered from his injuries and has been released from hospital.
The passenger in the Jeep, who goes by the street name Tweety according to Menga's family, is in police custody.
Toronto police are not commenting on the case because of the ongoing SIU investigation.
